annotations.title: Built an Altar.
annotations.text: [1] Noe without expreſs commandment, and without delay, offereth Sacrifice to God, for the benefite receiued in his and his families conſeruation, with the other liuing creatures, in that general deluge of the world, VVel knowing (ſaith S. Ambroſe) [2] that to be true thankſgiving, which is preſented, not commanded [3] : therefore he made no delay [4] . For the virtue of a grateful mind excludeth doubtful deliberation, and he that expecteth til the debt of thanks be exacted, is an ungrateful perſon. [5] For more ſolemnitie, he dedicated an apt and permanent place, for this peculiar diuine ſervice, building an Altar to our Lord. The Hebrew word Mizbeach (of the verbe Zabach, to kil, or make ſacrifice) and the Greeke Thyſiaſterion, ſignifie an Altar to ſacrifice on [6], not a common table for meate. He offered of the [7] cleane and beſt things: becauſe pure and deuout Sacrifice is due to God. Moreouer, it was large and bountiful [8], for he offered of all the kinds of cleane beaſts and fowls. Finally, he offered them in Holocauſts [9] , where all was burned and conſumed in the honour of God. [10] How grateful all this was to God, Moyſes ſignifieth ſaying: Our Lord ſmelled a ſvveete ſauour: not that either anie ſweete corporal ſauour could of it-ſelfe delight God, who is the moſt ſpiritual ſubſtance, or that the burning of flesh, bones, and bowels of beaſts could yeld ſweete ſauour; but the deuout mind declared by ſuch external dutie greatly pleaſed God. For God requireth both, but ſpecially a ſincere heart. As not only diuine Scriptures and holie Fathers [11], but alſo moral Philoſophers teach vs. It were a grievous thing (ſaith Plato writing of ſacrifices) If God had reſpect rather to the gifts and ſacrifices of men, then to their mind. lib. peri tes proſeuches.

notes.text: Sacrifice is pleasant to God: not for the external things but for the sincere mind.
Leuit. 1. Psal. 50. Isaie 1. Amos. 5. Mal. 1. Iust Mar. li 3. q. 4. S. Hiero. Q. Heb.
